title: introduce-keyspace-spill-prober-and-fidelity-aware-replayer
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: In production we observed intermittent tail regressions that correlated with sudden expansion of active keyspace driving K/V cache spill events on GPUs. Existing workload runners focus on steady-state sequence mixes or bursty arrival patterns but do not explicitly exercise the interaction between expanding keyspace, eviction churn, and CPU/GPU memory page behavior. This PR introduces two cooperating test artifacts: 1) a Keyspace Spill Prober (ksp-prober) that drives controlled, configurable keyspace expansion and spill pressure against the serving runtime, and 2) a Fidelity-Aware Replayer that records traces from a target cluster and replays them while injecting spill events to measure metric sensitivity and identify thresholds where quality or latency regress.

Design/Implementation: - ksp-prober: Go binary under benchmark-lab/cmd/ksp-prober. Generates sequences with a parameterized key cardinality curve (linear, exponential, and randomized ramps) and per-sequence eviction hints. The prober supports three modes: dry-run (no model calls, validates traffic shaping), sampling (periodic short requests with real model calls), and saturate (sustained ramp until eviction rate stabilizes). It exposes a small HTTP admin port for health and dynamic parameter adjustments. - fidelity-replayer: Python tool under benchmark-lab/tools/fidelity_replayer.py. Consumes existing trace exports (protobuf or ndjson), attaches synthetic KV keys to tokens via a configurable hash function, and replays the traffic against an instrumented endpoint while toggling explicit cache-seed/evict calls (simulated via SDK hooks). The replayer collects token-level latencies, eviction counts, model output deltas (via deterministic prompt hashing), and anomaly markers. - Telemetry & reporting: Adds a new exporter plugin (benchmark-lab/exporters/kv_spill_reporter) which emits per-epoch CSV/JSON that include: epoch_start, epoch_end, active_keyspace_size, eviction_rate, p50/p95/p99 gen latency, token-invalidation-count, and output-regression-score. The reporter is designed to be consumed by existing bench dashboards.

Test Plan and Baseline Results: - Added unit tests for simulation curves and admin API (Go: 3 new tests). - Integration tests run in CI using a containerized runtime image (lightweight LLM shim) to validate end-to-end replay mechanics. - Local experiments on a staged cluster: exponential ramp to 2x active keyspace produced a median eviction increase from 0.3/s to 4.1/s and p95 latency degradation of ~18% in the saturate mode; in sampling mode the fidelity-replayer detected output delta > 0.02 (cosine similarity drop) when eviction_rate > 2.2/s for the small RAG-like prompt set used.

Commits Summary: - feat(ksp-prober): initial Prober CLI with linear/exp/random ramp models
- feat(fidelity-replayer): trace ingestion + synthetic key attachment + SDK replay hooks
- feat(exporter): kv_spill_reporter with CSV/JSON outputs
- test: unit tests and lightweight integration job
- ci: add workflow and matrix for replay scenarios
- docs: README with usage examples and tuning guide (benchmarks/kv_spill/README.md)

Changed files (high level): - benchmark-lab/cmd/ksp-prober/main.go (new): CLI, ramp generators, admin API - benchmark-lab/tools/fidelity_replayer.py (new): trace parser, replay loop, SDK adapters - benchmark-lab/exporters/kv_spill_reporter/producer.go (new): reporting pipeline - benchmark-lab/benchmarks/kv_spill/README.md (new): how-to and tuning - benchmark-lab/.github/workflows/kv-spill-ci.yml (new): CI matrix for small/large traces - benchmark-lab/tests/integration/test_ksp_scenario.sh (new): integration smoke - benchmark-lab/Cargo.toml / go.mod updates (minor)

Review conversation (high-level): - Diego (reviewer): "Can we make the prober's default ramp conservative? I hit cluster pressure in my dev box." -> Author: "Default changed to sampling mode and exposed --ramp-curve to avoid surprise." - Anika: "The reporter should export a stable key for correlating runs; add a run_id and deterministic seed." -> Author: "Added run_id and deterministic seeding option; also documented in README." - Leo: "Consider adding a non-LLM shim mode for CI to avoid external model calls." -> Author: "Added lightweight LLM shim for CI and a small trace fixture (10k tokens) so the CI matrix stays fast."

CI Summary: - Unit tests: pass - Integration: CI runs with LLM-shim (matrix: small/medium traces) - Lint: gofmt/golangci-lint warnings fixed - Performance matrix: recorded ephemeral perf metrics stored in artifacts (CSV) Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2024-11-12 after CI green and 2 approvals.

Impact and how to use: - This PR gives SREs and perf engineers a reproducible way to provoke and measure KV cache spill behavior and quantify when spills begin to materially affect latency and generation fidelity. - Usage: deploy ksp-prober in sampling mode against a canary cluster; capture trace, then run fidelity-replayer with --inject-evict-thresholds to locate knee points. - Future work: integrate reporter outputs into the perf dashboard for automated regression detection and add a GPU memory-pressure simulator to approximate real spill costs on clients without GPU access. Related: ENG-1462 (investigate tail regressions), ENG-1503 (k/v cache instrumentation enhancements).

release_notes: Add Keyspace Spill Prober (ksp-prober) to simulate expanding active keyspace pressure
Add Fidelity-Aware Replayer for trace-driven regressions with injected spill events
New kv_spill_reporter exporter for CSV/JSON metrics consumable by dashboards
notes: Designed for benchmark-lab consumers; emphasizes reproducible end-to-end experiments for KV eviction-related regressions. Kept runtime impact low by default (sampling mode).
